focus: gearCardThing scoping and the skipHidden condition in StatPart_Entad; cache safety
diffSource: since the oldest restore point still kept (2026-10-03T21:08:30Z); older ones were pruned, so the chat's first changes may be missing

findings.title: displayExcludesHidden skips hidden traits on every stat, so MaxHitPoints is cached without its hidden factors
findings.detail: skipHidden is true for any stat while displayExcludesHidden is set. Vanilla InfoTextLineFromGear calls gear.LabelCap under that flag. GenLabel reads t.MaxHitPoints, which is GetStatValue(MaxHitPoints, cacheStaleAfterTicks 10) on a cacheable stat (Stats_Basics_General.xml:18). So hovering a pawn stat stores a MaxHitPoints that leaves out hidden trait factors and offsets, and the game reads it for up to 10 ticks. The label also shows a wrong HP percentage, which reveals the hidden trait. MarketValue also loses UnidentifiedMarketValue under the flag. One change at StatPart_Entad.cs:21: `bool skipHidden = offsetsViaWearer && (EntadWearerStats.displayExcludesHidden || EntadWearerStats.gearCardThing == req.Thing);`. StatOffsetFromGear, the only call the flag is meant for, always has offsetsViaWearer true, so nothing intended is lost. The 'nothing computed under the flag is cached' comment on Patch_InfoTextLineFromGear is wrong for the same reason.

findings.title: StatPart_Entad is added after StatDef.SetImmutability, so some affected stats stay immutable
findings.detail: PlayDataLoader calls ResetStaticDataPost (StatDef.SetImmutability) at line 276, before StaticConstructorOnStartupUtility.CallAll at line 346. A stat with no parts that is not in mutableStats keeps immutable=true and its immutableStatCache after InjectStatParts adds the part. Items cache their first value permanently, and a pawn wearer stat ignores entad gear being put on or taken off. After stat.parts.Add(part) in InjectStatParts, set stat.immutable = false and call stat.Worker.SetCacheability(false).

findings.title: TraitsChanged clears the comp caches but not the game's stat caches; RemoveTrait misses the removed trait's stats
findings.detail: TraitsChanged drops propertyFactors and wearerOffsets but never calls ClearStatCaches, so an AddTrait or RemoveTrait that doesn't touch MaxHitPoints leaves cached values for the item and its holder stale. Permanently so for immutable stats (see the previous finding), since ClearCacheForThing is the only thing that clears immutableStatCache (StatWorker.cs:1373). In RemoveTrait the trait is removed from activeTraits before RescaleHitPoints calls ClearStatCaches, so its own stats are never cleared. Call ClearStatCaches() in RemoveTrait before activeTraits.Remove(trait), and in TraitsChanged.

findings.title: HasVisibleOffset compares (total - hiddenPart) against float.Epsilon
findings.detail: CompEntad.WearerOffset builds total and hiddenPart as two separate float sums. When the revealed traits cancel out (for example +0.1 and -0.1) on top of a hidden one, total - hiddenPart can leave rounding noise far above float.Epsilon (1.4e-45). GearAffectsStat then returns true and the gear shows up under 'Relevant gear' as +0.00, the exact symptom this file exists to remove. Use a tolerance at EntadWearerStats.cs:125, e.g. !Mathf.Approximately(total, hiddenPart) or a 1e-4 threshold.

findings.title: Stats getter publishes the HashSet before filling it
findings.detail: The getter assigns stats = new HashSet<StatDef>() and only then fills it, so a re-entrant or concurrent first call can see an empty set. statFlags would then be built from it once and stay wrong for the whole session. AffectsStat and IsEntadGear already build into a local and publish at the end; doing the same here (build a local set, then assign stats) makes all three caches consistent.

findings.title: gearCardThing also covers def-level comp rows inside ThingDef.SpecialDisplayStats
findings.detail: WithGearCard sets the flag around every MoveNext, and that includes comps[i].SpecialDisplayStats(req). Vanilla never computes a wearer pawn stat there: ThingDef.SpecialDisplayStats only calls GetStatValue for RangedWeapon_WarmupMultiplier and RangedWeapon_RangeMultiplier, which are not wearer stats. But if a third-party CompProperties row calls the wearer's GetStatValue, StatWorker.GetValue writes that pawn's temporaryStatCache with HidingFor(gear) true, so the cached number lacks the hidden offset. Nothing in the corpus does this today; worth one comment line so a later change keeps the scope narrow.

findings.title: GearAffectsStat postfix scans comps instead of using the IsEntadGear flag table
findings.detail: Patch_GearAffectsStat calls gearDef.GetCompProperties<CompProperties_Entad>(), a list scan, when the gearFlags index lookup is right there. It only runs while an explanation or hyperlink list is being built, so the cost is small; this is a consistency point, not a performance one.
